reading: Each colour-3 hollow shape has a one-cell stub on one side. A mirror copy of the shape is drawn on the opposite side, reflected across the row/column just beyond the body (one-cell gap). The copy is colour 1 when the reflection is left/right and colour 8 when it is up/down.

slots.subject: each colour-3 object (body plus one-cell stub)
slots.axis: the line one cell beyond the body edge opposite the stub
slots.colour: 1 for horizontal reflection, 8 for vertical reflection

why: every object has exactly one stub; the copy is its exact reflection, and nothing else changes

reading: The grid is split into a few large single-colour regions sprinkled with single noise cells of one colour. The output is a 1x1 grid holding the colour of the region that contains the most noise cells.

slots.score: number of noise cells inside each region
slots.output: 1x1 grid of the colour of the region with the highest score

why: on every pair the output colour is the region with strictly the most noise cells

reading: Several rectangular outlines and many scattered single cells of other colours. Each outline's interior is filled with a checkerboard (starting at the interior top-left) of the scatter colour whose cell count equals the checkerboard's cell count; all scattered cells are erased.

slots.colour: scatter colour whose count = number of checker cells in that frame's interior (ceil(area/2))
slots.pattern: checkerboard anchored on the interior top-left cell
slots.rest: scattered marker cells cleared; outlines kept

why: each frame is assigned the unique marker colour whose count matches its checker capacity

reading: A single 1 at the bottom-left corner launches a diagonal line upward that bounces between the left and right borders until the top; all other cells become 8.

slots.source: the single colour-1 cell at bottom-left
slots.path: one cell up per row, column zig-zags reflecting off left/right borders

why: each row has exactly one 1, adjacent rows differ by one column, reversing at the borders

reading: The top-left 3x3 block (enclosed by an L of 5s) is a key pattern. Somewhere else in the noisy grid the same 3x3 pattern appears exactly; a 5x5 ring of colour 5 is drawn around that occurrence.

slots.key: input rows 0-2, cols 0-2 (bounded by the 5 L at row 3 / col 3)
slots.target: the other 3x3 window whose cells exactly equal the key
slots.drawn: the 1-cell ring around that window, colour 5, overwriting whatever was there

why: exactly one other window equals the key; only its surrounding ring changes
invariants: all cells outside the ring unchanged

reading: The grid is a set of thick single-colour stripes (vertical or horizontal) with noise cells. Every stripe is cleaned to its majority colour: each column (vertical stripes) or each row (horizontal stripes) is set to its most common colour.

slots.direction: the stripe orientation (columns in pairs 0,1; rows in pair 2)
slots.line: each column or each row along the stripe direction

why: output equals per-column majority (vertical stripes) or per-row majority (horizontal stripes)

reading: A colour-5 vertical line in column 4 splits the grid. The right half is mirrored onto the left half and overlaid (non-zero cells fill zeros); the output is the left 4 columns.

slots.right: cols 5-8 reversed left-right, overlaid onto left where left is 0

why: output row = left row with zeros replaced by the mirrored right row

reading: A 1 region sits above a 6 region with a jagged boundary. In the column where the 1 region reaches deepest, all 1 cells become 9; in the column where the 6 region peaks highest (rightmost on ties), all 1 cells become 4.

slots.valley column: column with the lowest 1 cell -> its 1 cells recoloured 9
slots.peak column: column with the highest 6 cell (tie: rightmost) -> its 1 cells recoloured 4

why: only 1 cells in those two columns change

reading: A small colour-2 template sits in a 0/5 noise grid. Copies of the template are stamped in colour 2 into places where its shape fits entirely on 0 cells; not every fitting slot is used (pair 0 skips one, pair 1 skips two that overlap other stamps), so the selection rule is unclear.

slots.anchors: positions where every template cell lands on a 0 cell (a subset; selection rule unknown)

why: every added 2 belongs to a full copy of the template lying on former 0 cells

reading: Each colour-3 block spawns two diagonal staircases of copies: repeatedly shifted down by its height and left (and right) by its width, continuing until off the grid.
why: every added cell is part of a copy of a block offset by k*(height, +/-width), k>=1
